# OpenCode Telegram Bot

A Telegram bot that acts as a bridge between **Telegram** and **[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)**. You send a message to the bot, it forwards it to OpenCode's local API, and the AI response is sent back to you — all from your phone.

It can also download videos with **yt-dlp** and, instead of sending the file, hand the
**transcript** to OpenCode AI so it can answer questions about the video in Bengali or English.

Send it a **file** and it asks which folder should keep it, then hands that file and your next
message to OpenCode. Ask for a **screenshot** and it captures the machine it runs on and sends
the picture back.

---

## The ways to use it

### 1. Download a video (simplest)

```
/download https://youtu.be/xxxx
```

That is it. No question asked — the bot downloads the video and sends it straight back as a
Telegram video. `/dl`, `/d` and `/ডাউনলোড` do the same thing.

If you would rather not paste the link in the same line, type `/download` on its own and the
bot asks for the link, then starts downloading as soon as you send it.

### 2. Ask OpenCode AI about a video

```
/ask https://youtu.be/xxxx এই ভিডিওতে কী বলা হয়েছে?
```

The bot does **not** download the video. It pulls the title, channel and subtitles with yt-dlp,
hands them to OpenCode together with your question, and posts the answer back. The AI replies
in whichever language you asked in.

### 3. Just send the link

Send a bare link and the bot asks what you want:

```
🔗 Link received
What should I do with it?
আপনি কি ভিডিওটা ডাউনলোড করব, নাকি OpenCode AI-কে জিজ্ঞাসা করবেন?

[⬇️ Download] [🤖 Ask OpenCode AI]
[❌ Cancel]
```

Tap a button, or just type one word — in Bengali or English:

| You type | What happens |
|---|---|
| `download`, `dl`, `save`, `ডাউনলোড`, `নামাও`, `নামিয়ে দাও` | Downloads and sends the video |
| `ai`, `opencode`, `ask`, `সারাংশ`, `অনুবাদ`, `বলো` | Sends the transcript to OpenCode AI |
| `cancel`, `no`, `বাতিল`, `না` | Drops the link and clears the cache |
| anything else, e.g. `এইটা কী বিষয়?` | Treated as a question about the video, answered by the AI |

### 4. Send a file, then tell OpenCode what to do with it

Send the bot any file — a document, photo, video, audio, voice note or animation — and it asks
where the file should live:

```
📎 annual-report.pdf
application/pdf · 1.2 MiB

Where should I save it? Each button shows the folder it means.

📂 Project: /home/me/code/project
🎵 Audio:   /home/me/Music
🎬 Video:   /home/me/Movies

You can also type project, audio, video or any folder path.

[📂 Project
/home/me/code/project]
[🎵 Audio
/home/me/Music]
[🎬 Video
/home/me/Movies]
[🗑 Cancel]
```

Tap a button, or type `project` / `audio` / `video`, the Bengali equivalents, or a full path such
as `~/Downloads`. The name is kept as `annual-report (1).pdf` if the folder already has one, so
nothing is ever overwritten.

Once it is saved the bot asks what to do with it, and **your next message is handed to OpenCode
together with the file's path**:

```
✅ Saved annual-report.pdf to /home/me/code/project/annual-report.pdf

What should I do with it?
ফাইলটা সেভ হয়েছে — এখন কী করব?
```

```
summarise this and list the three biggest numbers
```

OpenCode reads the file at that exact path — no download, no second copy — does the work, and
replies in the language you used. If it needs a tool that is missing, it says so instead of
guessing. `/cancel` at any point drops the question; a file that was already saved stays put.

| Folder | Comes from | Default |
|---|---|---|
| 📂 Project | `WORKSPACE_PATH` | the folder the bot runs in |
| 🎵 Audio | `ATTACH_AUDIO_DIR` | `~/Music` |
| 🎬 Video | `ATTACH_VIDEO_DIR` | `~/Movies` |

Files waiting for an answer are held for 15 minutes, then deleted.

### 5. `/screenshot`

```
/screenshot
```

The bot captures the screen of the machine it runs on and sends the picture back, so you can look
at a desktop or headless box from your phone. `/ss`, `/shot` and `/স্ক্রিনশট` do the same.

Which command it uses depends on the machine:

| Machine | Tried in order |
|---|---|
| Termux | `termux-screenshot` (needs the Termux:API app), then the Screenshot Tile app |
| Linux (Wayland) | `grim` first, then the rest below |
| Linux / BSD | `scrot` → `maim` → `grim` → `spectacle` → `gnome-screenshot` → `import` |
| macOS | `screencapture` |
| Windows | PowerShell with `System.Drawing` |

**Every capture is saved first, then sent.** The file lands in a `Screenshot` folder next to the
bot (`./Screenshot/Screenshot_20260930-105723.jpg`), and that is the copy you get in Telegram —
nothing is deleted afterwards. Set `SCREENSHOT_DIR` to keep them somewhere else. A capture over
10 MB is sent as a file instead of a photo.

If nothing on the machine can take a screenshot, the bot asks OpenCode what to install and reports
the answer — it never invents a command.

On Termux the usual install is:

```bash
pkg install termux-api   # then grant the screenshot permission once
```

Without Termux:API the bot falls back to the **Screenshot Tile** app
([cvzi/ScreenshotTile](https://github.com/cvzi/ScreenshotTile)), which captures on its own and is
triggered over a broadcast:

```
am broadcast -a com.github.cvzi.screenshottile.SCREENSHOT -e secret 1234 com.github.cvzi.screenshottile
```

The app has to be installed: the bot asks `pm list packages` first and skips the broadcast if the
package is missing. Because that app saves the picture where its own settings point, the bot
watches those folders (`Pictures/Screenshot`, `Pictures/Screenshots`, `Pictures/ScreenshotTile`,
`Pictures`, `ScreenshotTile`, `Screenshots`, `DCIM/Screenshots`, `Download`), waits for the new
file, copies it into `./Screenshot` and leaves the app's own copy alone. Point `SCREENSHOT_TILE_DIR`
at the app's folder if you keep yours somewhere unusual, and set `SCREENSHOT_TILE_SECRET` if you
changed the secret from `1234` in the app.

---

## How downloads work

```
You (Telegram) ──/download <link>──▸ Bot ──yt-dlp──▸ video file
                       │                               │
                       ◂──────── sendVideo ────────────┘
```

`yt-dlp` is managed by the bot itself, following the same update mechanism the
[YTDLnis](https://github.com/deniscerri/ytdlnis) Android app uses:

1. Ask the GitHub releases API for the latest build (`yt-dlp`, `yt-dlp-nightly-builds` or
   `yt-dlp-master-builds` depending on `YTDLP_UPDATE_CHANNEL`).
2. Compare `tag_name` against the installed version — no download if they match.
3. Pick the release asset that suits this machine, download it, test it, and only then
   replace the managed binary.

Step 3 is the part that has to know where it is running. Node reports a target such as
`android/arm64` on Termux, and each target gets its own ordered list of assets:

| Machine | Tried in order |
|---|---|
| Termux (`android/arm64`) | `yt-dlp` → `yt-dlp_linux_aarch64` → `yt-dlp_musllinux_aarch64` |
| Linux x64 | `yt-dlp_linux` → `yt-dlp_musllinux` → `yt-dlp` |
| Linux arm64 | `yt-dlp_linux_aarch64` → `yt-dlp_musllinux_aarch64` → `yt-dlp` |
| macOS | `yt-dlp_macos` → `yt-dlp` |
| Windows x64 / arm64 | `yt-dlp_x86.exe` / `yt-dlp_arm64.exe` |
| Anything else | `yt-dlp` |

The `*_linux*` and `*_macos*` builds are PyInstaller executables linked against glibc,
which is why Termux leads with the plain `yt-dlp` zipapp and only keeps the native
builds as a fallback for a device with no python3. Set `YTDLP_ASSET` in `.env` to pin
one exact asset name and skip the guessing.

The binary lives in `BOT_DATA_DIR/bin/yt-dlp`, separate from anything on your `PATH`, so
`pip install -U` elsewhere cannot break a download in progress. The asset that won is
remembered in `state.json`, so the same machine never downloads the same build twice.
Three things are handled automatically:

- **Bootstrapping** — if no yt-dlp exists at all, the bot installs one with
  `python -m pip install yt-dlp` (falling back to `pkg install`).
- **Termux shebangs** — the release asset starts with `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, which cannot
  execute on Termux because there is no `/usr/bin`. The bot rewrites the shebang to the
  python3 it actually found.
- **Wrong builds** — a candidate that downloads but will not start is discarded and the
  next one is tried; if none run, the working copy is kept and nothing is broken. The
  downloaded bytes are checked against the release's sha256 when GitHub publishes one, and
  the new file is `rename`d over the old one only after `--version` succeeds on it.

If the GitHub API is rate-limited, the bot falls back to `yt-dlp --update-to`, which does not
use the API for the download. That self-update rewrites the managed file with the published
asset, so the shebang is repaired again afterwards and the result is probed; if it no longer
starts, the bot drops back to the yt-dlp on your `PATH` instead of failing downloads.

Set `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `.env` to raise the API limit from 60 to 5000 requests an hour.

### The cache never accumulates

- Every job gets a throwaway directory that is deleted as soon as it finishes, whether it
  succeeded or failed.
- A sweep runs every 2 minutes and removes anything left behind by a crash, but never touches a
  job that is still running.
- The file is deleted right after Telegram accepts it, so the disk returns to where it started.
- The sweep also runs on startup and on clean shutdown.

Set `KEEP_DOWNLOADS=true` if you would rather keep a copy after sending, and `/cleancache` to
empty the cache by hand.

### Large videos

Telegram refuses uploads over 50 MB. Rather than failing silently, the bot reports the real
size and offers three choices: send it as a plain file, save it to
`~/Downloads/telegram-ytdl`, or drop it. Lower `YTDLP_MAX_HEIGHT` (say `480`) if you would
rather keep everything under the limit.

---

## How It Works (Big Picture)

```
You (Telegram) ──message──▸ Bot ──HTTP POST──▸ OpenCode (localhost:4096)
                                                        │
You (Telegram) ◂──reply──── Bot ◂──response───────────┘
```

1. You type a message to the bot on Telegram.
2. The bot receives it via Telegram's polling API.
3. It forwards the text to the OpenCode server running on your machine.
4. OpenCode processes the prompt and returns a response.
5. The bot sends that response back to you on Telegram.

If OpenCode is not running yet, the bot starts `opencode serve` for you and waits until it is ready.

### Seeing that it started

Every launch prints a coloured banner with the bot name, OpenCode URL, workspace, yt-dlp
version and cache path. Paths are shortened to `~/…`. Colour turns off automatically when the
output is not a terminal (piping to a file, for instance); set `FORCE_COLOR=1` to keep it.

When `OWNER_ID` is set, the bot also sends you a short "online" notice in Telegram on every
start, so you can confirm it came up without looking at the terminal. If Telegram refuses it —
which happens until you have sent `/start` to the bot yourself — the terminal says so instead.

### Long-running tasks

Agent runs are not capped at a fixed timeout. The bot sends the prompt asynchronously and
watches for the reply, so a task that takes ten minutes is fine. While it works you get a
progress preview every 15 seconds, and if nothing has changed for 45 seconds it tells you
OpenCode may be waiting on a permission approval.

Because the wait happens in the background, the bot stays responsive — you can send
`/tail`, `/stop`, `/restart` or `/logout` while a task is still running.

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Minimum Version | How to Check |
|---|---|---|
| **Node.js** | 18+ | `node --version` |
| **npm** | (comes with Node) | `npm --version` |
| **OpenCode** | Latest | `opencode --version` |
| **Python 3** | 3.8+ | `python3 --version` |
| **ffmpeg** | any | `ffmpeg -version` |

> Python and ffmmpeg are only needed for downloads. The bot installs yt-dlp itself on first run.

> **Don't have Node.js?** Download the LTS installer from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/).

---

## Step-by-Step Setup

### 1. Clone or Download This Project

```bash
cd path/to/this/folder
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
npm install
```

This installs:
- **grammy** — the library that talks to the Telegram API.
- **dotenv** — loads your settings from a `.env` file.

### 3. Create a Telegram Bot (Get Your Bot Token)

1. Open Telegram and search for **@BotFather**.
2. Send `/newbot` and follow the prompts to choose a name and username.
3. BotFather will give you a **token** that looks like `123456789:ABCDefGhIJKlmNoPQRsTUVwxyz`.
4. Copy that token — you'll need it in the next step.

### 4. Get Your Telegram User ID

Search for **@userinfobot** and press start — it replies with your numeric user ID.
Setting this means only you can talk to the bot.

### 5. Configure the Bot

Copy the example env file and edit it:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

```dotenv
BOT_TOKEN=YOUR_BOT_TOKEN_HERE
OWNER_ID=YOUR_TELEGRAM_USER_ID
WORKSPACE_PATH=
OPENCODE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4096
OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=
```

| Variable | What It Is |
|---|---|
| `BOT_TOKEN` | The token you got from BotFather |
| `OWNER_ID` | Your Telegram user ID. When set, everyone else is ignored. Blank = anyone can use the bot |
| `WORKSPACE_PATH` | Folder OpenCode uses as its working directory. Blank = the folder you run the bot from |
| `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` | Where OpenCode's HTTP server is listening |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | Optional. Only needed if you start `opencode serve` with a password |
| `YTDLP_UPDATE_CHANNEL` | Which release feed to follow: `stable`, `nightly` or `master`. Default `stable` |
| `YTDLP_ASSET` | Optional. Pin one exact release asset, e.g. `yt-dlp_linux_aarch64`. Blank = the bot picks per machine |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Optional. Raises the release API limit from 60 to 5000 requests an hour |
| `ATTACH_AUDIO_DIR` | Where a sent file goes when you pick 🎵 Audio. Default `~/Music` |
| `ATTACH_VIDEO_DIR` | Where a sent file goes when you pick 🎬 Video. Default `~/Movies` |
| `ATTACHMENT_MAX_MB` | Optional. Telegram never hands a bot more than 20 MB, so this is capped at 20 |

> `.env` is gitignored — your token is never committed.

### 6. (Optional) Secure the OpenCode Server

Without a password, anything running on your machine can drive OpenCode. To require
HTTP basic auth, set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` in `.env`. The bot sends it as basic
auth, and the server it auto-starts inherits the same password.

Note the password must match the server that is actually running: if OpenCode is
already up without a password, the bot's authenticated requests will be rejected.

### 7. Run the Bot

```bash
npm start
```

You should see:

```
OpenCode already running at http://localhost:4096.
Bot v0 starting as @yourbot — polling...
```

The bot is now live. Open Telegram and start chatting with it.

---

## Bot Commands

| Command | What It Does |
|---|---|
| `/start` | Shows a welcome message |
| `/download <link>` | Downloads the video and sends it back. Also `/dl`, `/d`, `/ডাউনলোড` |
| `/download` | Asks for the link, then downloads it when you send one |
| `/ask <link> [question]` | Sends the transcript to OpenCode AI and posts the answer |
| *(send a file)* | Asks where to save it, then hands the saved path to OpenCode with your next message |
| `/screenshot` | Captures this machine's screen and sends the picture. Also `/ss`, `/shot`, `/স্ক্রিনশট` |
| `/cancel` | Drops the pending link or file and empties the cache |
| `/stopdl` | Cancels a running download |
| `/ytdlp` | Shows the yt-dlp version, machine target, release asset, quality cap and cache state |
| `/ytdlpupdate` | Forces a yt-dlp update now, re-installing the right asset for this machine |
| `/cleancache` | Empties the download cache by hand |
| `/newchat` | Clears the current session so the next message starts a fresh conversation |
| `/tail` | Streams the running task's output to a new message, updated every 15s |
| `/stop` | Aborts the running task. OpenCode stops working on it immediately |
| `/restart` | Restarts OpenCode if the bot started it. Use it when OpenCode stops answering |
| `/logout` | Shuts the bot down (and stops OpenCode if the bot started it) |
| *(any text)* | Forwards your message to OpenCode and returns the AI response |

The bot also stops cleanly on `Ctrl+C`.

> `/restart` only works for a server the bot started itself. If you launched
> `opencode serve` by hand in another terminal, the bot will say so — stop that
> one yourself and send `/restart` again.

### Watching or stopping a run

Long tasks are not capped at a fixed timeout. While a task runs you get a progress preview
every 15 seconds, and if nothing has changed for 45 seconds the bot says OpenCode may be
waiting on a permission approval.

- `/tail` opens a second message that keeps showing the current output, so you can scroll
  back and keep watching. It stops updating on its own when the task ends.
- `/stop` cancels the task. The original message turns into `Stopped.`, and OpenCode stops
  working on it.

Both work while a task is running — the bot never blocks waiting for a reply, so you can
send commands at any time.

## Troubleshooting

### "BOT_TOKEN is not set"
You skipped step 5, or `.env` is missing the value. Run `cp .env.example .env` and fill it in.

### "Bot failed to start: Unauthorized"
The bot token is wrong or was revoked. Get a fresh one from @BotFather.

### Bot doesn't respond to anything
`OWNER_ID` is set but messages come from a different account. Check your ID with @userinfobot.

### "OpenCode is not responding — starting: opencode serve"
That is normal on first run — the bot starts OpenCode and waits up to 30 seconds for it to
become ready. If it then fails, run `opencode serve` yourself to see the real error.

### "Bot failed to start: OpenCode did not become ready"
Start `opencode serve` manually in another terminal to see why it is not coming up.

### 401 from OpenCode
`OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` is set in `.env` but the running server has no password.
Restart OpenCode with the same password, or blank out the variable.

### Bot is not answering prompts
Send `/restart` — it restarts the OpenCode server the bot started. Then send `/newchat`
to drop the stuck session and start fresh.

### "/restart" says it cannot restart OpenCode
The running server was started outside the bot. Stop it in its own terminal
(`Ctrl+C`), then send `/restart` again.

### Bot is stuck on "Thinking..."
That means OpenCode has not finished. The bot keeps waiting up to 30 minutes and shows
progress along the way. Send `/tail` for a live view, `/stop` to cancel, or `/restart`
then `/newchat` to start over.

If the bot reports that it is waiting on OpenCode, the run is probably blocked on a
permission approval — approve it in OpenCode itself.

### Response is cut off
Telegram limits messages to 4096 characters. Long responses are automatically truncated with a `[truncated]` marker.

### "❌ Download failed. ERROR: [youtube] … This video is unavailable"
That video is gone, private, or region-blocked. Nothing is wrong with the bot.

### "ERROR: unable to download video data: HTTP Error 403"
YouTube is rate-limiting your IP after several downloads in a row. Wait a few minutes, or set
`YTDLP_MAX_HEIGHT` lower so the requests are smaller.

### "GitHub release API unavailable — letting yt-dlp update itself"
The unauthenticated GitHub API allows 60 requests an hour per IP, and `yt-dlp --update-to`
needs the same API to find out what "latest" is — so it usually fails too. Either way the
bot keeps working on the version you already have. Add `GITHUB_TOKEN` to `.env` to raise the
limit to 5000 an hour.

### "yt-dlp does not run here" / "No release asset runs on …"
Every asset for this machine was downloaded and none of them started, so the previous copy
was kept. The usual cause is a missing python3 for the zipapp: `pkg install python`, then
send `/ytdlpupdate`. If it persists, `/ytdlp` prints the machine target, the asset in use
and the order the bot tries them in.

### "/ask" says there are no subtitles
Some videos genuinely have no captions. The bot still answers from the title and description
and says so. Adding a subtitle language to `YTDLP_SUB_LANGS` does not help if none exist.

### Videos are too large for Telegram
Telegram caps uploads at 50 MB. Set `YTDLP_MAX_HEIGHT=480` to fetch smaller files, or use the
"Save to phone" button the bot offers.

### The file buttons came out wrong, or the file went somewhere odd
The three buttons always show the folder they mean, so compare the path on the button with the
path you expected. Once a file is saved you can change your mind: reply with any other folder,
type a new path, or use **Other folder** on the saved message. A file that is still waiting is
deleted after 15 minutes; one that was saved stays where it is unless you delete it or move it.

### "📸 No screenshot tool worked"
Nothing on that machine can capture the screen yet. The bot asks OpenCode what to install and
pastes the answer, and tells you what it already tried. On Termux that usually means:

```bash
pkg install termux-api
```

then open the Termux:API app once and allow screen capture. If you would rather not install
Termux:API, install the Screenshot Tile app instead — the bot finds it through `pm` and uses it
without any Termux package. On a headless Linux box, install `grim` (Wayland) or `scrot` (X11) and
make sure the bot can reach the display: a screenshot tool in a desktop session cannot see the
screen of a server without `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`.

### "📸 Captured with Screenshot Tile app", but no picture arrived
The broadcast went out and the bot waited 20 seconds for a new file, so the tile app either
declined it or saved somewhere the bot does not look. Check the tile app's own folder setting and
set `SCREENSHOT_TILE_DIR` to that path; if you changed the app's secret from `1234`, set
`SCREENSHOT_TILE_SECRET` to match.

### The `Screenshot` folder is full
Captures are kept on purpose, so `/cleancache` does not touch them. Delete the files yourself
(`rm ~/cc/telegram_bot-master/Screenshot/*.jpg`) or point `SCREENSHOT_DIR` at a folder you clean
up on a schedule.
